historical_record.description: A one-storey cottage stood on the site in the early 1880s, before the two-storey house that stands there now.

One of the oldest houses on the street: its occupant appears in the city directories at Clara and 17th from 1884, the year a declaration of homestead was filed on the 26 by 126 foot lot. It was 56 Clara Avenue until the street was renamed in 1909.

Cutting Clara Avenue down to its official grade left the two-storey house four feet from a twenty-foot clay bluff, and after heavy rain in November 1893 creaking joists and cracked plaster drove the household out.
